svg.title: TOPAK H6 — A certified proof: every obligation accounted for by the route that closed it
svg.desc: "All N obligations proved" is the word of whichever backend discharged each obligation. A certified run (ADR-0046 A1, Batch 28) takes the same proof again and does not take that word: Z3 is not run, cvc5 stands behind spec/smt-checked and an SMT obligation counts only with a proof of false that the ethos checker accepted; every Zenon proof is re-checked by Isabelle; and spec/proof-cert.sh puts every obligation on exactly one route. Nineteen of the twenty-two proof modules certify; three do not (G10 §2.9). Three words, kept apart (ADR-0046 §1, A1): TLC checks mutations and witnesses; the prover proves invariants under named hypotheses; a proof is certified when every obligation is closed by the prover's normalization, by a checked proof, or by LS4. A certified proof is not a verified one (G10 §8), and none of it is a claim about the running reference (T-0045-28). Beside it, proposed: twelve of these modules' theorems proved again in Lean, of re-encodings, with the temporal step a kernel-checked induction and no SMT solver; the three that do not certify among them (ADR-0053; H7).
svg.text: TOPAK · H6

text.tspan: A certified proof: every obligation accounted for by the route that closed it

svg.text: "All N obligations proved" is the word of whichever backend discharged each obligation. A certified run (ADR-0046 A1, Batch 28) takes the same proof again and does not take that word: Z3 is not run, cvc5 stands behind spec/smt-checked and an SMT obligation counts only with a proof of false that the ethos checker accepted; every Zenon proof is re-checked by Isabelle; and spec/proof-cert.sh puts every obligation on exactly

one route. Nineteen of the twenty-two proof modules certify; three do not (G10 §2.9). Three words, kept apart (ADR-0046 §1, A1): TLC checks mutations and witnesses; the prover proves invariants under named hypotheses; a proof is certified when every obligation is closed by the prover's normalization, by a checked proof, or by LS4. A certified proof is not a verified one (G10 §8), and none of it is a claim about the running

reference (T-0045-28). Beside it, proposed: twelve of these modules' theorems proved again in Lean, of re-encodings, with the temporal step a kernel-checked induction and no SMT solver; the three that do not certify among them (ADR-0053; H7).

text.tspan: Accepted · C2, C4 · ADR-0046 E2 and A1, Batch 28, 2026.10.04

svg.text: The method is adopted by ADR-0046 A1; spec/proof-certification.md, which describes it, is itself a draft and not a record. Its wrapper, driver, method and every result are the drafter's, regenerated at ratification by the assistant at the custodian's direction (B28).

text.tspan: 1 · Why a second run: whose word is "All N obligations proved"?

svg.text: tlapm itself
"trivial": the obligation is closed by normalization, with no backend
Z3 4.8.9, the default SMT solver
Nobody. Z3 4.8.9 emits no proof the prover reads
Zenon 0.8.4
A proof script in Isabelle's language
Nobody, unless asked (-C)
Isabelle2025
A proof, checked by Isabelle's kernel as it is made
Isabelle
LS4
unsat, for a step of temporal logic

The prover stops at the first backend that answers. In the sixteen proof modules of 2026.10.04 about a third of all obligations were SMT's, "so a third of every 'proved' was Z3's unsupported word" (proof-certification.md §1).

text.tspan: checks Zenon's proofs, and nothing else (ADR-0046 E2)

svg.text: ADR-0046 as ratified at B25 said tlapm "can hand every SMT-proved obligation to Isabelle for checking (-C)". It cannot. -C checks the scripts Zenon emits and nothing else. For a module whose obligations are all SMT's it
hands Isabelle a theory with no lemmas, and Isabelle reports "No errors found": true, and says nothing.

Seen by reading the generated theory for RunConfinement_proof: fourteen lines, no lemma. Run over every proof module on 2026.10.04 (proof-method.md §5a: thirteen of sixteen were in that position or close to it).

E2 corrects the sentence and says -C does not move T-0045-31's residual. A checked SMT route does: A1. G10 lists it among the results the drafting did not anticipate (§3, result 9); the sentence was the drafter's and was not
checked before B25.

text.tspan: 2 · The certified run: every obligation on exactly one route (proof-certification.md §2, §4)

svg.text: spec/proof-cert.sh <Module>_proof > <Module>-proof-cert-results-<date>.txt runs tlapm -C --cleanfp --strict --toolbox 0 0 --solver '<smt-checked> "$file"', then reads the prover's per-obligation messages, which name the backend that discharged each one, and the wrapper's verdicts. A module is certified when every obligation is on one of the first five rows. The counts are the sums over the twenty-two certified results
files (§3 below).
the driver (proof-certification.md §4)
--cleanfp: nothing is carried over from an earlier run, an
uncertified one least of all.
Within the run the prover reuses a result for an obligation
identical to one just proved; the driver counts those, so SMT
obligations less the reused ones never exceed the calls
forwarded on an accepted proof.
STRETCH=n multiplies the backend timeouts; the file states it.
CVC5= and ETHOS= default to the floor gates' binaries under
tools/.
Exit status non-zero unless the module is certified.
every obligation on exactly one row (§5)
Certified: "All N obligations proved. X of them rest on tlapm's own
normalization or on a checked proof; Y rest on LS4, whose answer no
checker confirms."
Not certified: "NOT CERTIFIED: <reason>".
The header fixes the modules of the EXTENDS chain, the prover, and the
wrapper, solver, checker and signature, each by digest: a change to any
is a different certification.
Evidence not tracked: one query and one proof per SMT obligation,
about 30 KB an obligation. The file carries a digest of the sorted (query,
proof) digest pairs, which a rerun reproduces (the custodian's decision,
Dated, never edited; a changed module or proof gets a new run.
Anchor-proof-cert-results-2026.10.04.txt: a difference in any
line is a difference in the module, the proof, the prover, the solver, the
checker, the signature or the wrapper, and the header says which (§6).

text.tspan: Trivial: closed by tlapm's own normalization, with no backend

svg.text: About two obligations in three. Nothing is sent anywhere: the prover's front end closes it.
Trusted as written: tlapm's normalization is a premise (§8).
Counts. On trust in tlapm.
The prover writes one SMT-LIB query per obligation it sends to SMT and runs the configured solver on it. The
wrapper forwards unsat only on a proof the checker accepted; otherwise unknown, and the obligation passes
on to Zenon and then Isabelle.
The floor's checker (T-0045-14), with a wrapper of its own binding the proof to the prover's query,
as floor/cvc5-checked binds one to cedar symcc's (ADR-0030 §5 A1).
Counts. A proof of false from the query's own declarations and
assertions.

text.tspan: Zenon, its script checked by Isabelle (

svg.text: What no SMT answer closed goes on to Zenon. Operators_proof has two ENABLED goals there that Isabelle
accepted; RulesFloorNV_rev5_proof has five, the cases of BaseNext, under Z3 as under cvc5, and Isabelle
refuses one.
A script Isabelle refuses, or cannot check, is not a checked proof: the module does not certify.
Counts when Isabelle confirms it.
10: 9 accepted, 1 refused
The prover's last backend, tried after SMT and Zenon.

text.tspan: Isabelle's kernel, as the proof is made

svg.text: Isabelle is still trusted, for its own proofs and for checking Zenon's (§8).

text.tspan: LS4: the temporal step of each theorem

svg.text: One to three per theorem, of one fixed shape: "the invariant holds initially and every step keeps it, so it holds
always" (PTL).

text.tspan: No route checks a temporal step

svg.text: Reported separately in every results file's last sentence: "N rest on LS4, whose answer no
checker confirms".
Counts, and is reported as not certified.

text.tspan: Anything else: failed under the checked backends, an SMT answer with no accepted
proof, a Zenon proof Isabelle refused or could not check

svg.text: unknown from the wrapper reads as "this backend did not prove it". An obligation no checked route closes is a
missing check, not a counterexample.
The run is refused as a whole: proof-cert.sh exits non-zero and the file ends NOT CERTIFIED:
<reason>.
6 failed, in two modules; and the 1 refused Zenon proof above
Under the digest of its text: q-<digest>.smt2.
Adding only --produce-proofs --dump-proofs --proof-format-mode=cpc
--proof-granularity=dsl-rewrite.
cvc5's proof begins by restating them; the wrapper drops those and writes declarations
derived from the query. A proof about other symbols would no longer type-check.
Each assume step, its abbreviations expanded, must equal one of the query's
assertions structurally. Anything else is refused.
Against the CPC signature in tools/cpc/. Only correct makes the wrapper print
unsat; anything else, its own errors included, prints unknown.

text.tspan: Why the two are the same formula

svg.text: (! φ :named N), (! φ :pattern (…))
A name is a label; a pattern is an instantiation hint and no
part of what the formula says
(forall ((x S)) φ), x in φ
The proof format's bound variable. The wrapper rewrites
the query into this form, scope by scope, and compares
exactly; never the other way, so a bound variable and a
constant of one name cannot be confused

text.tspan: What it refuses, and what it writes

svg.text: A query form it does not carry into a proof (anything but set-logic, set-option, set-info, declare-sort, declare-fun, declare-const, assert,
check-sat, exit); a let; a binder it does not read; a proof step other than an abbreviation, assume, assume-push, step, step-pop; a proof that assumes
nothing. Each refusal recorded with its reason.
Per query: q-<digest>.smt2, the proof as checked .cpc, and a verdict .json with the digests of query, proof, solver and checker; one line per call in
calls.log.
A solver's sat or unknown needs no certificate: it can only pass the obligation on or fail the proof.
honest
Runs cvc5
Forward unsat
checker accepted the proof
other
Proves the query with (assert false) added
Forward unknown
an assume is not one of the query's assertions
empty
Says unsat, prints an empty proof
Forward unknown
proof assumes nothing
cut
An honest proof with its last step removed
Forward unknown
checker refused: the last step did not prove
false
spec/smt-checked-selftest.sh, against any query the prover wrote (tlapm --debug tempfiles keeps them). All four behave as required: the second is the case
step 4 exists for; the fourth shows the checker doing work. The wrapper is the one new piece of code the method trusts, so it is the one with a test that tries to make it
accept what it should not.

proof-certification.md §9 reports twenty modules and 5,084 obligations on 2026.10.04 (trivial 3,330; SMT 1,621; Zenon 10, nine accepted and one refused; Isabelle 2; LS4 115; failed 6); the two successors certified on 2026.10.05 add 141 and make the totals above. Time-outs ×10 is STRETCH=10: it recovered one obligation in Confinement and none elsewhere (§10).

text.tspan: 4 · The three that do not certify, and why restructuring them is deferred

svg.text: 262 obligations: five are Zenon's (the cases of BaseNext, lines 115 to 126), under Z3 as under cvc5, and
Isabelle refuses the script for one (obligation 55). The 10.02 results never ran the check.
What it would take: smaller steps for those cases, so that SMT proves them or Zenon's script reconstructs.
Cited by ADR-0026, ADR-0033 and ADR-0046 §4.
502 obligations: three, large type-invariant steps (TypeOK at lines 97, 102 and 190), are proved by Z3 and by
nothing else. cvc5 does not prove them at ten times the timeout or under five instantiation strategies.
What it would take: the steps split, by field or by action, in a successor module.
Frozen; cited by ADR-0034 and ADR-0046 §4.
503 obligations: the same three. Its proof is its predecessor's with one case split changed (Declared <= 1), so
it inherits the steps cvc5 cannot do.
What it would take: the same.
Frozen from G9; ADR-0033 A7 cites it.
All three are cited by digest in accepted records, so restructuring means successor modules; the custodian
deferred that on 2026.10.04 (ADR-0046 A1; G10 §7 item 74).
A refused script and an unproved obligation are missing checks, not counterexamples. The uncertified
results stand as they did: every obligation proved under the prover as first configured, on the residual of
T-0045-31 as first written, the SMT solver's soundness included.
Item 74, "the SMT backends' proofs checked", is discharged for nineteen of twenty-two, by cvc5 and the ethos
checker and not by Isabelle, the checker it named.
Proposed, a second route (ADR-0053; H7): all three are also proved in Lean, every step kernel-checked, of a
re-encoding (RulesFloorNV_rev5.lean, Confinement.lean under a flag). That does not certify them; it
proves the same theorems again, on the encoding.

text.tspan: 5 · What a certified proof still trusts

svg.text: The SMT solver's soundness
No longer trusted. Its answer counts only with a proof the checker accepted
Zenon's soundness
No longer trusted. Its script is checked by Isabelle
The checker, its signature and the wrapper are trusted in the solver's place. These are the floor's T-0045-14, and the wrapper has
the test of §7
Isabelle
Still trusted, for its own proofs and for checking Zenon's
Still trusted. One to three obligations per theorem: the step from "holds initially and every step keeps it" to "holds always". No checker
confirms it. For twelve modules a Lean re-encoding does that step as a kernel-checked induction (ADR-0053, Proposed); it does not
change what this run certifies
tlapm's translation of an obligation into an SMT query
Still trusted, as cedar symcc's encoding is for the floor. The checker certifies that the query is unsatisfiable; that the query says what
the obligation says is the prover's
Still trusted. About two obligations in three are closed by it with no backend
The prover's expansion of definitions, of ENABLED, and of primes
Still trusted; part of the translation
"So certification removes the largest unexamined premise, the SMT solver, and leaves three: the prover's front end, its temporal backend, and the checker" (§8).
tlapm with Z3, Zenon, Isabelle and LS4
tlapm with cvc5 behind spec/smt-checked and the checker of T-0045-14, Zenon checked by Isabelle, Isabelle, and LS4. Z3 is not run
"All N obligations proved" means every obligation is a theorem under the module's assumptions
The same, and of every obligation discharged by SMT: a proof of false from the query's own declarations and assertions was accepted by the
checker
The prover's and each backend's soundness are unexamined; no backend's answer is checked
The prover's translation of an obligation into a query, and its normalization; LS4, for the temporal step of each theorem; the checker and its
signature, which are T-0045-14's. The SMT solver's soundness is no longer a premise, as it stopped being one for the floor at Batch 24
The prover's digest, in every proof results file
That, and the digests of the solver, the checker, the signature and the wrapper, in every certified results file
"A certified proof still trusts the prover's translation of an obligation into a query, its normalization, LS4, and the checker" (G10 §3,
what these checks are).
"Twenty-two modules' invariants are proved, nineteen with checked proofs, and nothing about the running reference is. A matching
trace is drift detection on tested paths; T-0045-28 stands" (G10 §8).
"A certified proof is not a verified one. The prover's translation, its normalization, LS4 and the checker are trusted as written"
"Nothing here is independently reviewed" (G10 §8): the method document, the wrapper, the driver and the results are the drafter's;
B28 was not reviewed by a reader other than the drafter (ADR-0029 A2.5).

The prover's and each backend's soundness are unexamined here, as TLC's is in T-0045-29 and the engine's in T-0045-3; no mutation of the prover is run, and the proof-checking backend (Isabelle) is not invoked on the SMT proofs. A

proof is of the module, not of what runs (T-0045-28) (B25) Since B28 a proof module may be certified (ADR-0046 A1; spec/proof-certification.md): cvc5 behind spec/smt-checked and the checker of T-0045-14 in place of Z3,

text.tspan: 6 · Writing proofs that certify, and what is still open
What the first twenty modules taught (§10)

svg.text: Most proofs certify unchanged: thirteen of the sixteen that existed when the method was first run, at the default timeouts. cvc5 proves what Z3 proved in the great majority of steps.
cvc5 is weaker than Z3 on very large single steps: the three failures in Confinement expand a type invariant with many record fields in one BY. Split such a step by field or by action.

Name the parts of a large action. Labels_proof states one lemma on the shapes a step can have, with the action's LET named part by part; all 216 of its SMT obligations certified at the default timeout.

Give the case split explicitly when an obligation quantifies over a set that has just grown. Both failures met writing Labels_proof and Emergency_proof were of this kind, and each was a real gap in the argument.

An ENABLED goal may go to Zenon, whose script may not reconstruct. A lemma that cannot be certified should not sit in a certified module: Emergency_proof's was removed and its fact left to a TLC witness.
A longer timeout rarely helps; run proof-results.sh first, then proof-cert.sh.
G10 §5 makes it a convention: a proof is certified or its results file says why not.

LS4. No route checks a temporal step. The steps are few and of one shape; a small fixed lemma library proved once in Isabelle could replace them. Since 2026.10.05 the Lean re-encodings are a route beside this one in which the step is
an induction the Lean kernel checks, at the price of the encoding (ADR-0053, Proposed).
The translation. Nothing here examines how the prover turns an obligation into a query.
One solver, one version. cvc5 1.4.0 is pinned by digest because the floor pins it. A newer cvc5 may prove the six obligations that fail, and would be a different certification.
